retainedAgainstPromotion.observation: The minimum closure is expressible by KFD-1, KFD-2, KFD-5, KFD-11, and the fixed Profile without a new identity, boundary, authority, lifecycle, or operation.
Removing the Candidate name leaves every bounded decision observation available through the existing closure.
Fusing the procedure into existing responsibilities remains coherent when structural, review, disposition, admission, and release roles stay explicit.
No independent non-KFD adopter demonstrates an irreducible recursive responsibility.
The Profile can reproduce structural reports but cannot select semantic truth or governance disposition.

conditionsThatWouldReopen: A fixed-root decision observation changes when the Candidate is deleted while the existing closure remains available.
A non-KFD adopter demonstrates a recursive responsibility that cannot be represented by the existing closure.
Fuse testing reveals unavoidable authority ambiguity despite explicit role separation.
The fixed package fails to reject root, predecessor, review, authority, package, or claim-boundary substitution.
handling: Retain this counterevidence with any no-new-kfd lifecycle request. A later reopening requires a new exact cut and cannot mutate this assessment.
claimBoundary: Counterevidence prevents promotion-by-omission. It does not itself decide no-new-kfd or foreclose a later independently evidenced Candidate.
